Control: Security policy is reviewed and approved every year
What I found: Policy POL-SEC-001 v1.3 was last reviewed on 2024-03-11. Policy 2.1 requires a review every 12 months, so it was due 2025-03-11 and is about 20 months overdue as of 2026-11-30. The 'Approved by' field is blank: no evidence of CTO or CEO approval.
Policy rule: 2.1: review every 12 months; approved by CTO or CEO
How I tested: Inspected the policy's document details; compared review date and approval against policy 2.1.

Control: Privileged access is reviewed every quarter
What I found: Q3 2026 review completed on 2026-09-30. All 25 privileged accounts across AWS, GitHub, Entra ID and NetLedger have a reviewer (system owner), a date and a decision. Meets policy 3.1 for Q3. Follow-up: request Q1 and Q2 2026 review evidence, which was not provided.
Policy rule: 3.1: quarterly review by system owner, recorded for every account
How I tested: Inspected the Q3 2026 access review export; confirmed reviewer, date and decision on every row.

Control: Access is removed within 1 business day when someone leaves
What I found: 2 terminated employees still have active privileged access as of 2026-11-30 (policy 3.2 requires removal within 1 business day). (1) Kevin Brandt, terminated 2026-10-16 (involuntary): AWS Production PowerUser and GitHub Maintainer still active, 45 days late. His AWS account logged in on 2026-10-29, 13 days AFTER termination: possible unauthorized access, escalated to Head of Security immediately as a potential incident. (2) Lisa Tran, terminated 2026-11-06: NetLedger Approver (can approve payments) still active, 24 days late.
Policy rule: 3.2: remove all access within 1 business day of termination
How I tested: Compared the HR termination list (04) against current privileged access (05); checked account status and last login after each termination date.

Control: MFA is required for all accounts
What I found: 4 accounts have no MFA. 2 are covered by approved exceptions with compensating controls (admin-breakglass: EX-2026-01; svc-backup: EX-2026-02), so they're acceptable. 2 are not: (1) j.morales (Sales) has been excluded from MFA since 2026-06-02 as a 'temporary' phone issue, nearly 6 months, with no approved exception. This same account was compromised by phishing on 2026-09-18 (INC-2026-007), and the corrective action to enforce MFA is still open. (2) svc-deploy (CI/CD service account) is excluded with no approved exception or documented compensating controls. Violates policy 4.1, 4.2 and 2.2.
Policy rule: 4.1: MFA for all user, admin and service accounts; 4.2 + 2.2: exceptions must be approved and recorded
How I tested: Filtered the Entra ID MFA export (06) for accounts without MFA; matched each against the security exceptions register (07) and the incident log (14).

What I found: Annual training: 99 of 120 employees completed (82.5%); 21 have not started, past the Oct 31 deadline in policy 5.2. New hires: 5 of 7 recent hires are past their 30-day deadline in policy 5.1 (start dates Aug 3, Aug 17, Sep 8, Sep 21 and Oct 12). The 2 most recent hires (Nov 9 and Nov 16) are still within their 30 days and are not exceptions.
Policy rule: 5.1: new hires within 30 days; 5.2: everyone by Oct 31 each year
How I tested: Counted completion in the 2026 training report (08); compared each new hire's start date + 30 days against 2026-11-30.

What I found: Four phishing simulations ran in 2026, one in each quarter: Feb 10, May 12, Aug 18 and Nov 10. Meets policy 5.3. Positive trend: click rate fell from 19% (Q1) to 9% (Q4) and the report rate rose from 26% to 47%.
Policy rule: 5.3: at least one phishing simulation per quarter
How I tested: Reviewed the 2026 phishing simulation log; confirmed at least one campaign per calendar quarter.

Control: Vulnerabilities are fixed within policy deadlines
What I found: 3 vulnerabilities are past their policy 6.2 deadlines with no risk acceptance: VULN-0388 (Critical, api-prod-02) open 63 days vs 15; VULN-0405 (Critical, customer-db-01, the customer database) open 47 days vs 15; VULN-0371 (High, vpn-gw-01) open 41 days vs 30. Not exceptions: VULN-0412 (Critical) is risk-accepted by the CTO until 2027-01-31 per policy 6.3, with the server isolated; VULN-0420 (Critical) is 6 days old, with a fix scheduled 2026-12-03, within the 15-day deadline.
Policy rule: 6.2: Critical 15 / High 30 / Medium 90 / Low 180 days; 6.3: CTO risk acceptance up to 6 months
How I tested: Calculated days open for every Critical and High finding in the 2026-11-30 scan (10) against policy 6.2 deadlines; checked notes for approved risk acceptances (policy 6.3).

Control: Production changes are approved before deployment
What I found: 2 of 15 sampled production changes (13%) violated policy 7.1: CHG-1043 (payment webhook) was deployed 2026-10-14 4:20 PM but approved 2026-10-15 9:30 AM, after deployment; CHG-1051 (database settings) was approved by its own author (b.okafor), with no independent review. Not an exception: CHG-1047 was an emergency change deployed 2026-10-29 2:15 AM and approved by the CTO at 8:40 AM, within 24 hours as policy 7.2 allows. The other 12 changes were approved by someone else before deployment.
Policy rule: 7.1: approved by someone other than the author before deployment; 7.2: emergency changes approved by CTO within 24 hours
How I tested: Sampled 15 production changes (Oct-Nov 2026, file 11); compared author vs approver and approval time vs deployment time; checked emergency changes against policy 7.2.

Control: Vendors are risk-assessed and reviewed every year
What I found: 3 vendors with customer data break policy 8.1/8.2: (1) PayLoop (Critical, payments): latest SOC 2 report period ended 2024-09-30, 26 months old; update requested 2026-10-02, no response. (2) MailRelay (High, customer names and emails): never risk-assessed, no SOC 2 report. (3) DataPipe (Medium, customer usage data and emails): onboarded 2026-08-25 with no assessment before onboarding. Compliant: CloudNest, SupportDesk and HireFlow have current reports (SupportDesk's expires after 2026-12-31, so request the next one now). Not in scope: SnackBox has no data access, so policy 8.1/8.2 doesn't apply.
Policy rule: 8.1: assessment before onboarding; 8.2: current SOC 2 report every 12 months (for vendors with customer or employee data)
How I tested: Reviewed the vendor inventory (12); for each vendor with customer or employee data, checked for a pre-onboarding risk assessment and a SOC 2 report period ending within the last 12 months.

Control: Incident response plan is reviewed and tested every year
What I found: All three parts of policy 9 fail: (1) the Incident Response Plan (IRP-001 v2.0) was last reviewed 2023-06-14, about 29 months ago vs a 12-month requirement (9.1); (2) the last tabletop exercise was 2022-11-03, about 4 years ago vs an annual requirement (9.2); (3) the corrective action from INC-2026-007 (Jordan Morales account compromise, 2026-09-18), 'enforce MFA for this user', is still open after about 10 weeks (9.3). See also C4.
Policy rule: 9.1: plan reviewed every 12 months; 9.2: annual tabletop; 9.3: corrective actions tracked to completion
How I tested: Inspected the IR plan details, tabletop history and 2026 incident log (14); compared dates against policy 9.1-9.3 and checked corrective action status.

Control: Backups are taken daily and restores are tested
What I found: No restore test was performed in 2026 (Jan-Nov), versus at least one per quarter under policy 10.2, so 3 required tests were missed. There is no evidence that backups can actually be restored, which is the main risk in a ransomware or data-loss event. Daily backups (policy 10.1) succeeded on 332 of 334 scheduled days (99.4%); one failed day each in March and August, a minor gap to investigate.
Policy rule: 10.1: daily backups; 10.2: restore test every quarter
How I tested: Reviewed the 2026 backup and restore log (13); totaled successful vs scheduled backups and checked for quarterly restore tests.

Control: Security logs are kept as long as policy requires
What I found: All 5 in-scope log sources (Entra ID, AWS CloudTrail, GitHub, CloudNest database audit, NetLedger) are sent to the SIEM, with 90 days searchable and 390 days total retention, meeting policy 11.1 and 11.2 (365 days required). The archive holds logs back to 2025-10-27, consistent with the SIEM go-live date.
Policy rule: 11.1: logs sent to SIEM; 11.2: keep 365 days, 90 days searchable
How I tested: Inspected the SIEM log source and retention configuration (15); compared retention periods against policy 11.2.

Control: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit
What I found: All 5 storage locations holding customer or usage data (customer-db-01/02, analytics-db-01, customer-uploads, backups) are encrypted at rest with AES-256 (policy 12.1). All endpoints require TLS 1.2 or higher (policy 12.2). Not an exception: the public-assets bucket is unencrypted, but it holds only public website images, not customer data, so policy 12.1 doesn't apply to it.
Policy rule: 12.1: customer data encrypted at rest (AES-256); 12.2: TLS 1.2 or higher
How I tested: Inspected encryption at rest for each CloudNest storage resource and minimum TLS versions (15); checked what data each resource holds against policy 12.1-12.2.
